_about: One template, two uses. This file drives the downloadable DOCX (tools/make-template.cjs), its PDF reading copy and the web preview on both prototypes. The limits are draft recommendations for Dr Roopesh Sitharan’s review: change them here.
title: APARN Research Progress Contribution
subtitle: One contribution for your SAR presentation and, if you choose, APARN’s year-end publication
dual: Prepare one research update for your SAR presentation and, if you choose, APARN’s year-end publication.

limits.note: Draft recommendations for review. Easy to change.

intro: Use this template to describe where your research is now. Work in progress is welcome: you do not need finished results. Replace the grey guidance text with your own words and keep the eight headings.

sections.title: Project or research title
sections.guidance: A clear working title. A subtitle is welcome.

sections.title: Authors and context
sections.guidance: Each author’s name; affiliation, or “independent practitioner”; and the country or region where the research takes place. Please leave out email addresses: contact details are collected separately and are not published.
fields: Country or region of research activity

sections.title: Research question, purpose or creative inquiry
sections.guidance: What are you asking, exploring or making, and why does it matter to you and to others?
sections.placeholder: Write about your question or inquiry here.

sections.title: Artistic practice, methods or approach
sections.guidance: How you work: media, materials, sites, collaborators and methods. Use the language of your own discipline.
sections.placeholder: Describe your practice and approach here.

sections.title: Current progress and emerging insights
sections.guidance: Where the work is now: what has happened, what you are noticing, and what is still in development.
sections.placeholder: Share your progress and what is emerging here.

sections.title: Next steps, questions and invitations
sections.guidance: What comes next, what you would like feedback on, and any collaboration you are looking for.
sections.placeholder: Note your next steps and questions here.

sections.title: Images or documentation
sections.guidance: One or two images, or stills from video, sound or performance work. For each, give a caption, a credit, and confirm you have permission to share it.

sections.title: References and links
sections.guidance: Up to five references or links, in any citation style used consistently.

presentation.title: From contribution to a 5–10-minute update
presentation.intro: Your talk is a short, lively version of the same contribution. Visual, performative and sound formats are welcome within the time.
presentation.note: Presentation length is subject to the programme.

instructions: Download the DOCX. It also opens in Google Docs, Pages and LibreOffice.
Replace each piece of grey guidance with your own text. Keep the eight headings.
Aim for about two pages: 400–600 words plus one or two images.
Add a caption, credit and permission note for every image.
Save as DOCX or PDF, named Surname_ShortTitle.docx (or .pdf).
Use the same file to prepare your 5–10-minute update, and attach it in the submission form.
